text: What do I need to do to view the minecraft box split grammar slide deck ?

To view the **Instant Architecture with Box-Split Grammars** slide deck, you just need **Python 3.10+** (no extra packages required) to run the built-in local server:

1. **Start the server** from your workspace (`c:\Users\thatp\Documents\projects\slothlab`) in PowerShell:
   ```powershell
   py box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py
   ```
   *(If `py` isn't available, use `python` instead. You can also pass `--port <number>` if port `8790` is already in use.)*

2. **Open it in your browser:**
   - **Direct link to the deck:** http://localhost:8790/explorables/box-split-grammars/
   - **Gallery view:** http://localhost:8790/explorables/

> **Note:** Opening [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/thatp/Documents/projects/slothlab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html) directly as a file won't render the full presentation—[serve.py](file:///c:/Users/thatp/Documents/projects/slothlab/box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py) dynamically wraps it with the slide engine and interactive assets.

There are two very likely culprits on Windows:

1. **Port `8790` conflict with the background server that just stopped:**
   This session had a background copy of [serve.py](file:///c:/Users/thatp/Documents/projects/slothlab/box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py) running on port `8790` until a moment ago (`23:49`), when it was canceled. On Windows, Python's `ThreadingHTTPServer` enables `SO_REUSEADDR`, so starting a second `serve.py` on `8790` while another instance holds it often appears to start cleanly without throwing an error—and then stops answering once the first instance exits.
   - **Fix:** Press `Ctrl+C` in your terminal and restart it:
     ```powershell
     py box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py
     ```
     Or test a fresh port to rule out any lingering socket:
     ```powershell
     py box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py --port 8791
     ```
     Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8791/explorables/box-split-grammars/`.

2. **`localhost` (IPv6 `::1`) vs `127.0.0.1` (IPv4) or `https://`:**
   [serve.py](file:///c:/Users/thatp/Documents/projects/slothlab/box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py#L363) binds specifically to IPv4 `127.0.0.1` (not IPv6 `::1`). Try opening:
   - **http://127.0.0.1:8790/explorables/box-split-grammars/**
   - Make sure the browser didn't auto-switch the URL to `https://` (the local server is plain `http://`).

If it still doesn't connect after restarting, paste the exact browser error (e.g. `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, `403`, or `404`) and what your terminal shows and I can pinpoint it immediately.

`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` means Chrome connected to port `8790`, then the socket closed without sending HTTP headers. On Windows, the most likely causes are:

1. **Test a fresh port (`8791`) first** — when our background `py.exe` launcher task (`task-160`) was canceled earlier, Windows can leave the child `python.exe` process holding port `8790`, and Windows `SO_REUSEADDR` lets your new `serve.py` bind `8790` silently without an error:
   ```powershell
   py box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py --port 8791
   ```
   Then open **http://127.0.0.1:8791/explorables/box-split-grammars/**.

2. **If `--port 8791` works**, check for a leftover listener on `8790` and stop it:
   ```powershell
   Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8790 -State Listen | Select-Object LocalAddress, OwningProcess
   ```
   Then run `Stop-Process -Id <OwningProcess>` on that PID.

3. **Check two quick Windows/browser gotchas** if `8791` also gives `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE`:
   - **Terminal paused (QuickEdit):** If you clicked inside the PowerShell window (so the title bar says `Select` or there's a white selection box), Windows freezes Python mid-request until you press `Esc` or `Enter` in the terminal.
   - **Terminal output:** Let me know if the terminal logs anything (a `GET ...` line or Python traceback) when you load the page, or stays completely blank.
